preconditions.description: The input contains at least one line (T).

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) for line in stdin.strip().splitlines())
preconditions.description: All lines in the input are strings.

preconditions.expression: int(stdin.strip().splitlines()[0]) == len(stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:]) if len(stdin.strip().splitlines()) > 1 else True
preconditions.description: The number of test cases T matches the number of subsequent lines.

preconditions.expression: all(s.count('W') == 1 and all(c in 'BW' for c in s) for s in stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case string contains exactly one 'W' and only 'B' or 'W' characters.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(line in ['Chef', 'Aleksa'] for line in stdout.strip().splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output line is either 'Chef' or 'Aleksa'.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda s: 'Chef' if (s[:s.index('W')].count('B') > 0) ^ (s[s.index('W')+1:].count('B') > 0) else 'Aleksa')(s) == out for s, out in zip(stdin.strip().splitlines()[1:], stdout.strip().splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the winner is 'Chef' if exactly one side of the white cell has black cells (XOR condition), and 'Aleksa' otherwise (both sides empty or both sides non-empty).
